steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on PIA, a method for animating personalized text-to-image images with text prompts. Cover the motivation, the challenges, how PIA works at a high level, and the AnimateBench benchmark.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Background: personalized T2I models and the lack of work on animating them
- Motivation and the two challenges (image alignment, motion controllability)
- Limits of existing T2V models and temporal alignment layers
- PIA: design and how it addresses the challenges
- Summary and AnimateBench evaluation

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Background
  - T2I generation democratized: Stable Diffusion community, explosion of personalized models
  - AI artists/enthusiasts share personalized models on Civitai, Hugging Face; affordable (e.g., laptop with RTX3080)
  - limited research on giving these personalized images dynamic motions
- Motivation and challenges
  - personalized images: distinctive styles, impressive visual quality -> worth animating
  - text prompts to guide animation -> streamline creative work, less effort
  - two challenges: image alignment with detailed personalized image; motion controllability through text
- Existing approaches
  - large-scale T2V models: videos from text or images, but can't preserve unique styles / high-fidelity details (no personalized domain knowledge)
  - temporal alignment layers: plug-and-play, turn personalized T2I into T2V, keep styles
  - adapting personalized T2V for image animation: layers mainly align appearance of frames in latent space -> hard to follow motion-related text prompts
- PIA (Personalized Image Animator)
  - built on base T2I model (Stable Diffusion) + temporal alignment layers from previous work
  - swap base T2I for any personalized T2I at inference -> personalized domain knowledge
  - trainable condition module in input layer: takes conditional image + inter-frame affinity (current frame vs conditional frame)
  - borrows appearance features from conditional frame guided by affinity hint -> better image alignment
  - fine-tune condition module + temporal alignment layers jointly, base T2I fixed
  - temporal layers can focus on motion-related alignment -> motion controllability
  - generalizes by replacing T2I with any personalized model; preserves distinct features, high-fidelity details
- Summary and evaluation
  - image alignment, motion controllability by text, flexibility with personalized models
  - engaging, customizable animation experience
  - AnimateBench: personalized T2Is, curated images, tailored motion-related prompts
  - extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations on AnimateBench

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Text-to-image (T2I) generation has recently been democratized and made incredible progress, thanks to the growing Stable Diffusion community and the explosion of personalized models. Lots of AI artists and enthusiasts create, share and use personalized models on model-sharing platforms like Civitai and Hugging Face, and they turn their imagination into images at an affordable cost (e.g., a laptop with an RTX3080). But there is still limited research that explores how to give these unique personalized images dynamic motions.

We are interested in animating personalized images because they have distinctive styles and impressive visual quality. Also, if text prompts are used to guide the animation, many creative tasks in the personalized community can be streamlined, with less effort needed. This task is promising but it has two distinct challenges: image alignment with the detailed personalized image, and motion controllability through the text prompt. Recent advancements in training large-scale text-to-video (T2V) models let users generate videos from text or images, but these approaches struggle to keep the unique styles and high-fidelity details of the conditional images, because they don't have personalized domain knowledge. To deal with this, researchers have developed temporal alignment layers. These are plug-and-play modules that turn personalized T2I models into T2V models and keep their distinct styles. There have been many attempts to adapt these personalized T2V models for image animation, but the integrated temporal alignment layers mostly focus on aligning the appearance of individually generated frames in latent space so the video is smooth. Because of that, they find it hard to animate images according to motion-related text prompts.

- PIA (Personalized Image Animator)
  - built on base T2I model (Stable Diffusion) + temporal alignment layers from previous work
  - swap base T2I for any personalized T2I at inference
  - trainable condition module in input layer: conditional image + inter-frame affinity as inputs
  - borrows appearance features from conditional frame guided by affinity hint -> better image alignment
  - fine-tune condition module + temporal layers jointly, base T2I fixed -> temporal layers focus on motion -> motion controllability
  - generalizes to any personalized model; keeps distinct features, high-fidelity details
- Summary and evaluation
  - image alignment, motion controllability by text, flexibility
  - AnimateBench: personalized T2Is, curated images, tailored motion-related prompts
  - extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Text-to-image (T2I) generation has recently been democratized and made incredible progress, thanks to the growing Stable Diffusion community and the explosion of personalized models. Lots of AI artists and enthusiasts create, share and use personalized models on model-sharing platforms like Civitai and Hugging Face, and they turn their imagination into images at an affordable cost (e.g., a laptop with an RTX3080). But there is still limited research that explores how to give these unique personalized images dynamic motions.

We are interested in animating personalized images because they have distinctive styles and impressive visual quality. Also, if text prompts are used to guide the animation, many creative tasks in the personalized community can be streamlined, with less effort needed. This task is promising but it has two distinct challenges: image alignment with the detailed personalized image, and motion controllability through the text prompt. Recent advancements in training large-scale text-to-video (T2V) models let users generate videos from text or images, but these approaches struggle to keep the unique styles and high-fidelity details of the conditional images, because they don't have personalized domain knowledge. To deal with this, researchers have developed temporal alignment layers. These are plug-and-play modules that turn personalized T2I models into T2V models and keep their distinct styles. There have been many attempts to adapt these personalized T2V models for image animation, but the integrated temporal alignment layers mostly focus on aligning the appearance of individually generated frames in latent space so the video is smooth. Because of that, they find it hard to animate images according to motion-related text prompts.

To address these limitations we introduce PIA, a Personalized Image Animator that is good at both image alignment and motion controllability. First, we build our framework on a base T2I model (i.e., Stable Diffusion) and add well-established temporal alignment layers following previous works. This way PIA can use personalized domain knowledge, since the base T2I model can be replaced with any personalized T2I model during inference. Second, to give the framework image animation ability, we add a trainable condition module into the input layer of the T2I model. This module is important for generating each frame of the animation, and it takes the conditional image and the inter-frame affinity between the current frame and the conditional frame as inputs. With this design the condition module borrows appearance features from the conditional frame, guided by the affinity hint, and this gives better alignment with the condition image. Finally, we fine-tune the condition module and the temporal alignment layers together while the base T2I model is kept fixed. Since the condition module in the input layer already improves appearance-related alignment, the temporal alignment layers can focus more on motion-related alignment, which improves motion controllability. Importantly, we show that PIA's animation capability generalizes easily when the T2I model is replaced with any other personalized model. This flexibility lets users animate their elaborated personal images with text prompts while keeping distinct features and high-fidelity details.

To sum up, PIA is a powerful solution for personalized image animation, with superior image alignment, motion controllability by text, and the flexibility to integrate various personalized models. This approach gives users an engaging and customizable animation experience. Since there is no benchmark for personalized image animation, we introduce a new benchmark called AnimateBench, which has various personalized T2Is, curated images and tailored motion-related prompts. To validate how effective PIA is, we did extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations using AnimateBench. These evaluations give a robust assessment of the capabilities and performance of our approach.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Recent democratization of text-to-image (T2I) generation has seen incredible progress, driven by the growing Stable Diffusion community [1,2] and the explosion of personalized models [3,4]. Numerous AI artists and enthusiasts create, share, and use personalized models on model-sharing platforms such as Civitai [5] and Hugging Face [6], turning imagination into images at an affordable cost (e.g., a laptop with an RTX3080). However, there is still limited research exploring how to infuse these unique personalized images with dynamic motions [7,8,9].

We are intrigued by the potential of animating personalized images, given their distinctive styles and impressive visual quality. Moreover, using text prompts to guide the animation process can significantly streamline various creative endeavors within the personalized community and minimize the required effort. While promising, this task presents two distinct challenges: image alignment with the detailed personalized image, and motion controllability through the text prompt. Although recent advancements in training large-scale text-to-video (T2V) models have enabled users to generate videos based on text or images [7], these approaches struggle to preserve the unique styles and high-fidelity details of conditional images due to the absence of personalized domain knowledge. To address this limitation, researchers have developed temporal alignment layers [9,8], plug-and-play modules that effectively transform personalized T2I models into T2V models while maintaining their distinct styles [9,8]. Despite numerous attempts to adapt these personalized T2V models for image animation [10,11], the integrated temporal alignment layers mainly focus on aligning the appearance of individually generated frames in latent space to ensure smooth videos. As a result, they find it hard to animate images according to motion-related text prompts.

To address these limitations, we introduce PIA, a Personalized Image Animator that excels in both image alignment and motion controllability. First, we build our framework upon a base T2I model (i.e., Stable Diffusion [1]) and incorporate well-established temporal alignment layers following previous works [8]. This allows PIA to leverage personalized domain knowledge by replacing the base T2I model with any personalized T2I model during inference. Second, to give our framework image animation ability, we introduce a trainable condition module into the input layer of the T2I model. This module plays a crucial role in generating each frame of the animation, taking the conditional image and the inter-frame affinity between the current frame and the conditional frame as inputs. Through this design, the condition module borrows appearance features from the conditional frame, guided by the affinity hint, resulting in improved alignment with the condition image. Finally, we fine-tune the condition module and the temporal alignment layers jointly while keeping the base T2I model fixed. Because the condition module in the input layer enhances appearance-related alignment, the temporal alignment layers can shift their focus towards motion-related alignment, leading to improved motion controllability. Importantly, we demonstrate the generalizability of PIA’s animation capability by replacing the T2I model with any other personalized model. This flexibility allows users to animate their elaborated personal images using text prompts while preserving distinct features and high-fidelity details.

In summary, PIA offers a powerful solution for personalized image animation, with superior image alignment, motion controllability by text, and the flexibility to integrate various personalized models, ensuring an engaging and customizable animation experience for users. To address the lack of a benchmark in personalized image animation, we introduce a new benchmark called AnimateBench, which comprises various personalized T2Is, curated images, and tailored motion-related prompts. To validate the effectiveness of PIA, we conducted extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations using AnimateBench, which provide a robust assessment of the capabilities and performance of our approach.
